subject: social_science

concepts.title: Farm and Non-Farm Occupations in Rural Areas
concepts.definition: Rural economies comprise agricultural work such as crop cultivation alongside diverse non-farm trades including craft-making, retail shops, repair services, and transportation.
concepts.key_idea: Rural livelihoods extend beyond crop cultivation to incorporate local service industries and craft production.
question_patterns: list the non-farm activities observed in rural villages like Kalpattu
what types of service jobs exist in agricultural settlements
identify non-agricultural sources of income in rural communities
how do villagers earn a living outside of crop farming
describe the variety of small shops and trades present in rural bazaars

solution_steps.explain: List non-farm work such as pottery, blacksmithy, weaving, shopkeeping, and repair work.
List crop cultivation activities like transplanting, weeding, and harvesting.

concepts.title: Wage Earners and Agricultural Labour Income
concepts.definition: Landless agricultural workers sell their manual labor during farming seasons for daily wages, facing low pay and lack of year-round employment.
concepts.key_idea: Agricultural labourers experience seasonal employment gaps and low wage rates due to landlessness.
question_patterns: calculate total income earned by an agricultural labourer over a given number of days
find the seasonal earnings of a landless farm worker
how much does a farm labourer earn when paid a specific daily wage for work days
compute total daily wage accumulation for seasonal transplanting or weeding
determine total wages earned from farm labour over a working period

solution_steps.action: multiply daily wage rate by number of days worked
solution_steps.explain: Total income is calculated by multiplying the wage rate per day by total days worked.

concepts.title: Small Farmers and Crop Loan Obligations
concepts.definition: Smallholders cultivate limited acreage primarily using family labour and often depend on trade loans for inputs, obligating them to sell produce below market prices.
concepts.key_idea: Small-scale agriculturalists face income shortfalls and trader loan commitments that reduce marketable surplus.
question_patterns: find the remaining paddy bags available for household consumption after repaying a crop loan
calculate paddy retained by a small farmer after settling input debts
determine surplus crop bags left after returning loan obligations in produce
how many crop bags remain for a smallholder after debt repayment
compute net harvested yield kept by a small farmer post debt settlement

solution_steps.action: subtract loan repayment bags from total harvested paddy bags
solution_steps.explain: Net retained harvest equals total harvested bags minus the bags given to the trader as loan settlement.

concepts.title: Causes and Dynamics of Rural Debt Trap
concepts.definition: A cycle of compounding debt occurs when crop failure or health emergencies force farmers to borrow repeatedly, exceeding their capacity to repay.
concepts.key_idea: High interest rates, bad seeds, monsoon failure, and distress borrowing lead to persistent rural indebtedness.
question_patterns: explain the factors that lead small farmers into a debt trap
what causes agricultural debt among rural households
how does crop failure contribute to persistent indebtedness
describe the cycle of borrowing faced by vulnerable cultivators
why are small farmers unable to repay loans from local moneylenders

solution_steps.explain: Pest attacks, inferior seeds, or drought cause crop failure and loss of earnings.
Inability to repay existing loans forces additional borrowing, creating an escalating debt cycle.

concepts.title: Large Farmers and Diversified Rural Enterprises
concepts.definition: Wealthy agrarian landowners operate large acreage, employ hired labor, and expand capital into processing mills, trade, and financial lending.
concepts.key_idea: Large farmers generate substantial surpluses enabling investment in off-farm commercial ventures.
question_patterns: how do large farmers diversify their income sources beyond crop cultivation
describe the role of big landowners in rural supply chains
what commercial businesses are typically owned by wealthy rural families
explain how large agrarian landowners utilize their surplus earnings
compare the economic status and business operations of large farmers with smallholders

solution_steps.explain: Large farmers cultivate extensive land holdings using hired labourers.
Profits are reinvested in mills, input supply shops, trading, and informal credit.

concepts.title: Categorization and Proportions of Indian Farmers
concepts.section: Agricultural Labourers and Farmers in India
concepts.definition: Indian agriculture is dominated by smallholders (80%) and landless laborers (40% of rural families), while large landholders comprise only 20% of farmers.
concepts.key_idea: Most cultivators in India operate marginal plots insufficient for full year-round subsistence.
question_patterns: calculate the number of small farmers in a region given the total farmer population
find the count of small landholders using the national eighty percent proportion
determine how many farmers belong to the small category out of a total population
compute the number of smallholders in an agrarian community
how many cultivators fall into the small farmer group in a given district

solution_steps.explain: Small farmers constitute 80 percent of the total farming population.

concepts.title: Terrace Farming and Community Labour in Hilly Regions
concepts.definition: Slope cultivation technique where hillside land is carved into stepped flat terraces with raised borders to retain water for paddy growth.
concepts.key_idea: Terrace carving enables hillside irrigation and rice cultivation through collective group labor.
question_patterns: describe the features and purpose of terrace farming in hilly areas
how does terrace cultivation retain water on mountain slopes
explain community labor practices in Nagaland terrace agriculture
why is terrace farming suitable for growing rice on hill slopes
what steps are taken to construct terrace fields in rural Nagaland

solution_steps.explain: Steps carved into hill slopes with raised mud borders retain water for paddy.
Villagers form small groups to clean, prepare, and cultivate hillside fields together.

concepts.title: Forest Gathering and Supplementary Rural Livelihoods
concepts.definition: Non-wood forest produce collection, livestock rearing, and dairy cooperative sales provide essential supplementary earnings for rural households.
concepts.key_idea: Rural families rely on natural resource gathering and animal husbandry to supplement seasonal farming income.
question_patterns: what non-farm forest goods are collected by rural communities for income
how do livestock and dairy sales supplement agrarian livelihoods
identify additional sources of income in forest-adjacent villages
describe the role of cooperative milk societies in rural earnings
explain how forest produce collection helps families survive agricultural lean periods

solution_steps.explain: Collection of mahua flowers, tendu leaves, and wild honey sold to local traders.
Selling cow milk to local dairy cooperatives for supplementary daily cash.

concepts.title: Coastal Fishing Economy and Revenue Share Calculation
concepts.definition: Maritime fishing livelihoods depend on equipment investment and daily auctioning of catch, where revenues are divided into designated functional shares.
concepts.key_idea: Fish catch proceeds are distributed among crew members and equipment owners, with seasonal fishing bans requiring lean-period loans.
question_patterns: calculate individual share value from total fish auction revenue divided into equal parts
find the per-share payout from daily catch earnings
determine income per share when fish auction revenue is divided into specified shares
compute the value of one share from total fishing auction proceeds
how much is each share worth when auction earnings are split equally

solution_steps.action: divide total auction revenue by total share count
solution_steps.explain: Each share value is calculated by dividing total auction earnings by total number of shares.
